solution:
(i) Integrate by parts with $u=\ln x$ and $dv=x^{-2}dx$, so $du=\frac{dx}{x}$ and $v=-x^{-1}=-\frac1x$:
$$\int\frac{\ln x}{x^2}\,dx=-\frac{\ln x}{x}+\int\frac{1}{x^2}\,dx=-\frac{\ln x}{x}-\frac1x+C=-\frac{\ln x+1}{x}+C.$$

Hence
$$\int_1^e\frac{\ln x}{x^2}\,dx=\left[-\frac{\ln x+1}{x}\right]_1^e=-\frac{\ln e+1}{e}+\frac{\ln 1+1}{1}=-\frac{2}{e}+1=1-\frac{2}{e}.$$

(ii) Substitute $t=\sin x$, so $dt=\cos x\,dx$:
$$\int\frac{\cos x}{\sin x\sqrt{1+\sin x}}\,dx=\int\frac{dt}{t\sqrt{1+t}}.$$

Now substitute $w=\sqrt{1+t}$, so $t=w^2-1$ and $dt=2w\,dw$:
$$\int\frac{dt}{t\sqrt{1+t}}=\int\frac{2w\,dw}{(w^2-1)w}=2\int\frac{dw}{w^2-1}.$$

Using partial fractions, $\frac{1}{w^2-1}=\frac{1}{(w-1)(w+1)}=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{1}{w-1}-\frac{1}{w+1}\right)$:
$$2\int\frac{dw}{w^2-1}=\int\left(\frac{1}{w-1}-\frac{1}{w+1}\right)dw=\ln|w-1|-\ln|w+1|+C=\ln\left|\frac{w-1}{w+1}\right|+C.$$

Substituting back $w=\sqrt{1+\sin x}$:
$$\int\frac{\cos x}{\sin x\sqrt{1+\sin x}}\,dx=\ln\left|\frac{\sqrt{1+\sin x}-1}{\sqrt{1+\sin x}+1}\right|+C.$$

(An equivalent form, using $\sqrt{1+\sin x}-1$ rationalisation, is $\ln\left|\dfrac{\sin x}{1+\sin x+2\sqrt{1+\sin x}+1}\right|$; the logarithmic form above is the cleanest.)
hints: For (i), integrate by parts with u=ln x.
For (ii), substitute t=sin x first, then w=sqrt(1+t).
The second substitution reduces it to a partial-fractions integral.
